title: Epithelial Cell Repopulation and Preparation of Rodent Extracellular Matrix Scaffolds for Renal Tissue Development
protocol: Prepare decellularization solutions.
Prepare 500 ml reverse osmosis water (ROH2O).
Slowly add 10 ml Triton X-100 to 990 ml ROH2O under rapid stirring for at least 10 minutes before use.
Prepare 1,000 ml Triton X-100, 1% (v/v) in ROH2O (separate volume).
Slowly add 5 ml SDS (20% stock solution) to 995 ml ROH2O under fast stirring for at least 10 minutes before use.
Prepare kidneys for decellularization.
Anesthetize the rat by intraperitoneal injection of pentobarbital (50 mg/kg body weight).
Examine the depth of anesthesia every 10-15 minutes during surgery.
Monitor respiratory function and heart rate to assess anesthesia depth.
Administer a supplemental dose of pentobarbital if the animal shows signs of inadequate anesthesia.
Perform a longitudinal midline abdominal incision to expose kidneys, abdominal aorta, and inferior vena cava.
Inject heparin (2,000 USP Units/kg body weight) into the penile vein.
Mobilize both kidneys by gentle dissection.
Carefully separate the kidney from perirenal fat while keeping the renal capsule intact.
Perfuse kidneys with cold saline through infra-renal abdominal aorta.
Insert a 24 gauge catheter into the renal artery and ligate it to the artery.
Gently perfuse the kidney with 10 ml of cold phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Immerse kidney in 25 ml PBS within a Petri dish.
Place the kidney in a -20 °C freezer for gradual freezing and cell lysis.
Thaw the frozen kidney at room temperature.
Gently perfuse the kidney with 10 ml of PBS to check for leaks in the ligated renal artery.
Re-catheterize the renal artery if leaks or significant resistance are observed.
Assemble the decellularization perfusion system as depicted.
Connect one 8-inch length of peristaltic pump tubing to two lengths of silicone rubber tubing (>36 inches).
Join segments of tubing using male Luer lock to 1/8” barbed adapters and a female Luer x female Luer adapter.
Insert an additional male Luer lock to 1/8” barbed adapter into the downstream end for attachment to the renal artery catheter.
Connect each peristaltic pump tubing segment to the 4-roller pump head using a large pump cartridge.
Hold the “Prime” button to fully prime each perfusion circuit with solution from the first reservoir.
Verify that no bubbles remain in the tubing and secure the upstream end below the liquid-air interface of the reagent reservoir.
Perform the decellularization protocol at room temperature.
Connect the renal artery catheter of each thawed kidney to the end of the perfusion circuit tubing downstream from the pump, ensuring no air bubbles are entrapped.
Adjust the pump drive to 5 ml/min and press the “Start” button.
Confirm perfusion by observing solutions dripping from the bottom of the organ.
Perfuse with 500 ml ROH2O at 5 ml/min for 1 hr, 40 min.
Perfuse with 1,000 ml 1% Triton X-100 at 5 ml/min for 3 hr, 20 min.
Perfuse with 1,000 ml 1% Triton X-100 at 1 ml/min for 16 hr, 40 min.
Perfuse with 1,000 ml 0.1% SDS at 5 ml/min for 3 hr, 20 min.
Perfuse with 500 ml ROH2O at 5 ml/min for 1 hr, 40 min.
Wash the glass bioreactor reservoirs and heads with warm, dilute dish detergent solutions.
Rinse thoroughly with tap water and then ROH2O.
Allow components to dry completely.
Apply a small volume (~5 ml) of siliconizing reagent to the bottom of each reservoir.
Ensure that reagent wets the entire bottom surface for several seconds.
Drain excess fluid.
Allow the reservoirs to dry in a fume hood at room temperature overnight.
Alternatively, dry the reservoirs in an oven at 100 °C for 30 min.
Cut two 25-inch lengths of 1/16 inch ID silicone rubber tubing.
Cut one 8-inch length of peristaltic pump tubing.
Cut one 4.25-inch length of 1/16 inch ID silicone rubber tubing.
Cut two 1-inch lengths of thick-walled 1/16 inch ID silicone rubber tubing.
Cut one 2-inch length of 1/4 inch ID x 0.5 inch outer diameter (OD) silicone rubber tubing.
Prepare ten male Luer lock to 1/8 inch barbed adapters.
Prepare two male Luer plugs.
Prepare two female Luer caps.
Prepare five female Luer x female Luer adapters.
Wash all tubing with warm, dilute dish detergent solutions.
Rinse thoroughly in tap water.
Rinse thoroughly in reverse osmosis water (ROH2O).
Allow them to dry.
Assemble perfusion circuits.
Slip 1 inch length of thick-walled 1/16" ID silicone rubber tubing over inlet Luer acceptor attached to the head of the bioreactor.
Place male Luer lock to 1/8" ID barb adapter into open end of tubing.
Repeat for the other inlet Luer acceptor.
Connect a female Luer cap to seal off port.
Connect each 25 inch segment of 1/16" ID silicone rubber tubing to the 8 inch segment of peristaltic pump tubing using male Luer lock to 1/8" ID barb and female Luer x female Luer adapters.
Connect one open end of silicone rubber tubing to the media perfusate outlet on the outside of the bioreactor head.
Connect the 4.25 inch length of 1/16" ID tubing to the opposite (inner) side of the media perfusate outlet on the inside of the bioreactor head.
Connect a male Luer lock to 1/8" ID barbed adapter to the remaining open end of the perfusion circuit tubing.
Connect a female Luer x female Luer adapter to the male Luer lock.
Connect the female Luer x female Luer adapter to the open male Luer lock leading into the inlet Luer acceptor on the bioreactor.
Ensure that no ports on the bioreactor lid are left open or exposed.
Tightly close the vacuum valve on bioreactor body.
Fit the bioreactor head over the reservoir body.
Sandwich an O-ring between the grooves of each component.
Place a metallic clamp over the interface to hold components together.
Connect a 0.2 micron vent filter to the vent port on the bioreactor head using silicone rubber tubing.
Open the vent valve.
Loosen the red screw cap on the bioreactor head slightly.
Prepare an autoclavable pouch containing Luer adapters and serrated specimen forceps.
Seal the pouch.
Autoclave the assembled bioreactors and male Luer plugs.
Fit the bioreactor head over the reservoir body with an O-ring sandwiched in between.
Place a metallic clamp over the interface to hold components together.
Connect a 0.2 micron vent filter to the vent port using silicone rubber tubing.
Open the vent valve.
Loosen the red screw cap on the bioreactor head slightly.
Autoclave Luer adapters and serrated specimen forceps in a pouch.
Prepare a 50 ml solution of 0.1% peracetic acid, 4% ethanol within a fume hood.
Mix thoroughly by repeatedly inverting bottle.
Place the mixed solution in a biological safety cabinet.
Sterilize 150 ml of 1x PBS by autoclaving.
Prepare 50 ml of DMEM/F12 medium supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% Pen-Strep.
Collect decellularized kidneys.
Place all items in a biological safety cabinet.
Ensure that the biological safety cabinet is fitted with working electrical sockets for the digital pump drive.
Alternatively, use an extension cord to connect the pump drive to external electrical sockets outside the cabinet.
Collect autoclaved bioreactors with attached perfusion circuits.
Collect autoclaved pouch containing Luer adapters and forceps.
Collect digital pump drive with attached 4-roller head and large pump cartridges (1 per perfusion circuit).
Complete the perfusion circuit as described under sterile conditions within a biological safety cabinet.
Connect a 3-way stopcock between the male Luer lock to 1/8' ID barb adapter near the media perfusate inlet and the female Luer x female Luer adapter.
Leave all three ports on the stopcock open.
Remove the red screw cap on the bioreactor head.
Pipette 50 ml of the 0.1% peracetic acid, 4% ethanol solution into the medium reservoir through the opening.
Connect the peristaltic pump tubing segment to the pump head using a large pump cartridge.
Adjust the flow rate to 5 ml/min and press “Start”.
Allow the circuit to prime until liquid fills the perfusion line and reaches the remaining open port of the three-way stopcock.
Plug the port using a male Luer plug.
Allow the circuit to fully prime until no air is observed in the tubing or on the inside of the inlet Luer acceptor.
Increase the flow rate temporarily if necessary to expel bubbles from the perfusion line.
Stop the pump drive when the circuit is fully primed.
Plug the female Luer end of the renal artery catheter into the male inlet Luer acceptor using sterilized forceps.
Ensure the connection is tight and no air remains in the catheter.
Allow the kidney to hang gently from the renal artery catheter without twisting or kinking it.
Tighten the metallic clamp holding together the bioreactor head and body to seal the reservoir tightly.
Close the red screw cap on the bioreactor head.
Sterilize kidneys by perfusing with 0.1% peracetic, 4% ethanol solution at 5 ml/min for 1 hour.
After sterilization, stop the pump and open the red screw cap.
Aspirate all of the solution from the bioreactor reservoir using a sterile Pasteur pipette.
Pipette 50 ml of fresh PBS into the bioreactor reservoir.
Close the screw cap and start the pump to continue perfusion.
After the final PBS rinse, aspirate PBS from the reservoir and pipette in 50 ml DMEM/F12 medium supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% Pen-Strep.
Close the screw cap and transfer the bioreactor with the attached perfusion circuit to a large-capacity incubator maintained at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Connect the bioreactor perfusion circuit to the pump, and perfuse the kidneys at 4 ml/min for at least 1 hour prior to seeding.
Warm sufficient volumes of DMEM/F12 (supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% Pen-Strep) and cell dissociating enzyme to 37 °C.
Prepare 10 ml cell dissociating enzyme and 10 ml DMEM/F12 per 175 cm² culture flask for lifting cells.
Prepare 5-10 ml DMEM/F12 per kidney to be seeded.
Collect a sufficient number of culture flasks for the desired seeding concentration (4 x 10⁷ immortalized human RCTE cells per kidney).
Lift cells from the flasks using cell dissociating enzyme.
Aspirate medium from flask and pipette 10 ml cell dissociating enzyme into flask.
Place flask in 37 °C incubator to expedite dissociation.
Check flask on a phase contrast microscope every 2 min until full dissociation of cells from flask surface is observed.
Take a sample of dissociated cell suspension for counting prior to pelleting.
Dilute the cell suspension with an equal volume of pre-warmed DMEM/F12 medium, and centrifuge at 232 x g relative centrifugal force (RCF) for  5 min.
Count the cells during centrifugation.
Dilute the obtained sample with an equal volume of Trypan Blue.
Pipette 10 µl into each end of a hemacytometer for counting.
Calculate necessary pellet dilution volume to obtain the desired seeding concentration (2 x 10^7 cells/ml).
After centrifugation, dilute the pellet with an appropriate volume of culture medium to obtain a final concentration of 2 x 10^7 cells/ml.
Draw up 2 ml of the seeding suspension into a sterile 5 ml syringe.
Transfer the perfusion bioreactor to a biological safety cabinet.
Turn the stopcock valve to close flow to the seeding port.
Remove the male Luer slip plug from the stopcock, and connect the syringe loaded with the seeding suspension.
Quickly transfer the perfusion circuit back to incubator.
Use the large pump cartridge to secure the peristaltic pump tubing segment to the pump head.
Close the stopcock valve port pointing toward pump.
Slowly inject the cell suspension into kidney, ensuring that the entire suspension is transferred from the syringe into the stopcock and perfusion line.
Turn the stopcock valve to close flow from the syringe.
Start the pump at 25 ml/min for 15 min.
Lower the pump flow rate to 4 ml/min after 15 min.
Exchange medium (100 ml volume) the following day and thereafter every two days.
Prepare resazurin reagent by dissolving 110.5 mg resazurin sodium salt in 100 ml of PBS under stirring.
Dilute the solution 1:10 by adding 5 ml of the resulting solution to 45 ml fresh PBS to create a 440 µM resazurin stock solution.
Filter-sterilize the resazurin stock solution using a 0.2 μm syringe filter.
Store the filtered stock solution in a light-protected 50 ml conical tube at 4 °C.
Prepare a 10% solution of resazurin reagent in culture medium (e.g., 5 ml resazurin stock solution + 45 ml culture medium) to create resazurin working solution.
Autoclave a 10 ml volume of the resazurin working solution in a light-protected container.
Aliquot 1 ml each of resazurin working solution, autoclaved resazurin working solution, and culture medium alone into separate 1.5 ml collection tubes.
Place the open tubes in the same incubator as the perfusion bioreactors.
Transfer the kidney perfusion circuit from the incubator to a biological safety cabinet.
Remove the screw cap from the bioreactor head.
Aspirate culture medium from the bioreactor reservoir using a Pasteur pipette.
Pipette 10 ml of resazurin working solution into the reservoir.
Close the screw cap and transfer the kidney perfusion circuit back to the incubator.
Start the pump at 4 ml/min and allow reagent to perfuse through the kidneys for exactly 1 hr.
After 1 hr, stop the pump and transfer the kidney perfusion circuit to the biological safety cabinet.
Collect the conditioned (partially reduced) resazurin solution.
Add 100 μl of conditioned resazurin solution, resazurin working solution, autoclaved working solution, and culture medium blank into a black 96-well assay plate.
Read fluorescence intensity using a spectrophotometer.
Calculate the percent reduction using the formula:
% reduction = 100 x {[FI(conditioned resazurin solution) - FI(ORM)] / [FI(RRM) - FI(ORM)]}.
Normalize results by multiplying % reduction by circulating volume (10 ml).
Divide normalized result by incubation time (1 hr).
